text:
jordan: @customer_acme thanks for the report — I see you hit 403 + high latency after the recent invoicing change. Can you share a single request_id from one of the failed attempts?
customer_acme: got it, one sample id: req_01FZ9X3YQ5ZZ7ABCD9 — also saw 5–10s tail latency on some requests, not steady.
jordan: perfect. Can you also paste the minimal curl you used (with auth header replaced) so we can reproduce?
customer_acme: here's the curl we used (token redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"Summarize invoice 2025-01-09 for user alice@example.com"}'
```
lee-billing: FYI — their account had a billing plan change around 2025-01-08 16:12 UTC, invoice id inv-9832. Could be related to auth scope refresh.
maria-eng: @jordan @lee-billing thanks. First steps: we need the server logs around req_01FZ9X3YQ5ZZ7ABCD9 and a sanitized debug bundle. @customer_acme can you run the collector script below (it strips PII) and paste the produced archive name?
```bash
# safe-collect.sh (run on client side)
set -e
mkdir -p safe-debug && cd safe-debug
# capture minimal network trace
tcpdump -w net.pcap -c 100 not port 22 || true
# save request body and headers (mask Authorization and emails)
cat <<'JSON' > raw_request.json
{"request_id":"req_01FZ9X3YQ5ZZ7ABCD9","auth":"Bearer <TOKEN>","body":"summarize invoice for alice@example.com"}
JSON
# scrub emails and tokens
sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/<EMAIL_REDACTED>/g' raw_request.json > request_sanitized.json
sed -E 's/Bearer [A-Za-z0-9._-]+/Bearer <TOKEN_REDACTED>/g' request_sanitized.json > request_sanitized2.json
tar -czf ../safe-debug-archive-$(date +%s).tgz . || true
```
customer_acme: ran it, uploaded safe-debug-archive-1700000123.tgz to the link you sent.
ops-bot: attach-file uploaded safe-debug-archive-1700000123.tgz by customer_acme (size 4.1MB)
jordan: received. Thanks. @sanitization-sre can you run the quick PII check on the archive and confirm nothing sensitive remains?
sanitization-sre: running local checks: grep for emails/creditcard/ssn patterns, scanning. Found one leftover email in net.pcap metadata — I'll redact and reissue a new archive.
maria-eng: while that's happening, I'll try to replay with a cached token and with an expired-scope token to reproduce 403 vs latency. If I can't reproduce, we'll ask for a curl with --trace-ascii.
lee-billing: also adding the billing change logs for inv-9832 to the thread — looks like a service hook to auth-provider triggered a token rotation for customers on the legacy plan. Might explain intermittent 401/403.
sanitization-sre: reuploaded safe-debug-archive-1700000245.tgz (sanitized). No emails, tokens replaced with <TOKEN_REDACTED>, IPs pseudonymized.
jordan: great. @maria-eng can you confirm whether req_01FZ9X3YQ5ZZ7ABCD9 shows up in our front proxy logs? If so, paste the proxied request_id and timing snippet.
maria-eng: proxied id prox_6a9f... timeline: accept 2025-01-09T16:22:05.123Z -> routed 16:22:05.128Z -> backend start 16:22:05.140Z -> backend end 16:22:11.512Z -> response 16:22:11.520Z. Backend processing ~6.372s. We'll check model queue and billing auth calls in that window.
jordan: 6.3s backend spend explains the tail latency. Are there corresponding auth refresh calls in that period?
maria-eng: yes — we see an auth token refresh with upstream auth service for the customer's account at 16:22:05.135Z. Resp from auth service 16:22:05.138Z was 200 but followed by a policy check to billing service which took ~5.9s (billing side).
lee-billing: opening ticket BL-521 to track slow billing policy check — looks like a cache miss after the plan change. We'll prioritize.
jordan: action items: 1) lee-billing to fast-track BL-521 and share ETA; 2) maria-eng to attempt replay with sanitized curl and trace to confirm repro; 3) ops to monitor for other request_ids with same pattern; 4) customer to keep the sanitized archive link (we have it).
jordan: also note for support docs — update the repro collection guide with the sed-based scrub example and ask customers to never paste raw tokens/emails.
customer_acme: thanks all. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
maria-eng: quick note — to reproduce locally I used this minimal curl with masked token and added --trace-time:
```bash
curl -v --trace-time --trace-ascii trace.txt -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN_REDACTED>" -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
maria-eng: trace confirmed billing call at ~5.9s, reproduces when billing cache miss forced.
lee-billing: rolling a cache warm fix now, will post roll status here.
ops-bot: deploy started @ 2025-01-10T00:12:04Z for billing/cache-warm-quickpatch
lee-billing: deploy green. Patch warms policy cache on plan-change webhook. Monitoring APM for 30m.
maria-eng: can confirm a clean replay post-patch (backend end ~80–120ms).
jordan: marking resolved for now pending 30m monitor. Closing note: saved sanitized debug archive name and tickets BL-521. Thanks everyone.
